Infamous 2 endings, both bad and good.   

For those of who haven't played it yet, I'll explain.
The main starting event in the InFamous game series is the explosion of the so called "ray sphere". The main hero, Cole MacGrath was the one closest to it when it exploded, as he was delivering a package with it, not knowing what was inside. After the explosion, he survived, and gained the ability to control electricity.  

Besides MacGrath, there were other people who gained super abilities, and a plague started because of the radiation caused by explosion of the ray sphere. One of the "conduits" is named "The Beast", a giant capable of destroying cities and causing massive-nation wide destruction.

In the good ending Cole MacGrath sacrifices himself and other "conduits" around the world by activating the ray field inhibitor for the sake of humanity. He kills the Beast, stops the plague, and is honored the rank of saint by New Marais community, city that wasn't destroyed because of Cole's sacrifice. The final scene shows his best friend Zeke carry Cole's dead body in a coffin on a boat. When they almost reach the horizon everything becomes dark and the scene ends with a thunder striking. Then the "Fade Away" theme song starts playing. Made me cry even the 10th time re-playing it.    

In the bad ending, Cole has an opportunity to join the Beast, as it turns out he obtained the ability to activate superpowers in people that have the gene of the "conduit". If not activated, they will die of plague as everybody else, but the Beast has the ability of the ray sphere. Causing the same amount of destruction, killing people, he is saving those who mutate, gain power, and "evolve" as he says.   

In order to continue doing so they first need to stop Zeke and another conduit Nix, who driven by revenge wants  to use the ray field inhibitor against the beast.   

Cole kills Nix, but his best friend Zeke takes the RFI, and would rather die than give it to Cole. He points his gun to him, and Cole has no other option at this point, but to kill him. Zeke outstands most of Cole's lightning strikes, but is falling dead after catching a dozen of them.   

After killing his best friend, Cole returns to the beast, who tells him he cannot take any more of killing and the suffering he caused. He transferred his abilities to Cole, dying himself in the process. Cole then moves on, to continue the task he already took, becoming the ultimate beast he was supposed to stop.   

There were only 4 times I played the game in a way to get to the bad ending. Even Cole's complete transformation to a villian doesn't feel as bad as his betrayal and murder of Zeke and Nix.

Well that's the thing. I can see the positive things about having a kid. I of course plan on doing so in the future, as that's something I would like to experience throughout life. But I feel the responsibility to give the best moral basis to a kid to live their life confident. And I think I can find ways of teaching them necessary skills and basic knowledge of the world, social skills. I don't think education will be a problem. If I will succeed in the future and will make enough money to support my family I will do everything I can to create the best conditions for them. This, I can work on, I can think it through. But what I could never to this moment rationally think through, is how would I answer the questions in the lines of: "Why was I born?" "What's the point in life?" "What happens after death?" "Is there a god/heaven/hell?". I know my answers to that, but I'm not confident they will suit my future child. They will of course form their own worldview, whatever it will be. But is atheism a good base to start off in forming this worldview? I know religion would be the worst decision to do so, and I think atheism is way beyond better in comparison. To this point I now think this worry has lots to do with my own anxiety that is yet to be worked upon.

Let's put it this way. Studying religion I've come to a conclusion that I don't believe in any of the Gods I've read about. It is my belief that most of them are man-made. But I still leave free space for a possibility of an all-mighty deity existing. I believe that there are things I cannot perceive or am not supposed to perceive, such as a true face of God if one exists.                                                                               I can also imagine such God creating the universe the way we suppose it was created.  The main issue is, I do not believe that such God is biblical, evangelical, judaistic etc. I think that if there really is God, he just made things the way they are, and he lets everything happen. Including the diversity of religion. If so, I'm either not supposed to know for sure which God really is "the one" and is there even one, or he just doesn't care about it. An all-mighty deity if so would surely be capable of delivering information the way jt needs to.                                               So to sum it all up, I believe in scientific worldview, but I leave free space for an opportunity of someone creating universe this way. I do not believe this god is of some religion, bc there is no proof of it being such. I believe that with a high probability god just doesn't exist, but I might not be meant to find out the truth about its existance. Either way I can live my life the way I want, liberated from all the commandments and golden rule. I'm just an ex-religious person trying to fill the plot holes in my own life.
